SEPTIC ARTHRITIS (NATIVE JOINT) WITH NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE

Treat presumptively also for Chlamydia trachomatis infection

(asymptomatic urethritis) and test for HIV.  Infection control will

report cases with N. gonorrhea isolated to the state department of health.

Sexual partners within 60 days should be referred for evaluation and treatment.

Parenteral therapy recommended until clinical improvement, then switch to oral

therapy to complete 1-2 weeks of therapy.

Susceptibility results are required to guide potential switch to an oral medicat

# Treatment for N. gonorrheae (Plus see below for Chlamydia treatment)

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for initial parenteral treatment

# ______________________________________________________________

# Concomitant treatment for C. trachomatis

Preferred treatment:

[Azithromycin 1000 mg PO once \($\) M](psozid2-azithromycin-1gm-po-once)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-azithromycin-1gm-po-once)

Alternative treatment:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 7 days \($\) DI](psozid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-7ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-7ds)
